refinement.detail: Searched and found none THAT THIS TICKET MAY APPLY. SM-05 is a measurement and its standing rule is FILE FINDINGS, FIX NOTHING -- so any refinement it found is filed rather than applied, and applying one would invalidate the measurement it is reporting. What the search DID surface, all filed and none applied: the ladder does not fit a subject that ships no model, with four of five top rungs structurally unreachable on a greenfield artifact (SM-05-DF-05); "score the LOWEST anchor the artifact fully satisfies" read literally yields 0 on every dimension, now rejected by four judges across two rounds (SM-05-DF-05); D3's anchors have no referent rule, so "the domain" is ambiguous on a repository-scale subject and D3 spans two points between judges (SM-05-DF-06); and `check`'s citation grammar rejects the annotated citations judges actually write (SM-05-DF-07). Every one is a change to `references/eval_scorecard.md` or to `score_tools.py` -- the instrument this ticket is measuring ON -- and every one requires a version bump with its own measured discontinuity, which is the card's own change rule. That is the same ground SM-04 gave for not fixing SM-04-DF-06, and it holds harder here because SM-05 is the round the anchors were finally tested against a subject that could exercise them.

ticket.objective: The epic's product and a MEASUREMENT. Score the toolchain's removal on the card with two blind judges, D2 anchor 3 exactly as written. IF D2 REACHES 3 OR 4, the subjects were the problem and five epics of greenfield fixtures could never have exercised the card. IF D2 IS STILL 2 ON A GENUINE MEASURED SIMPLIFICATION, the card cannot measure complexity and D2 must stop being cited -- having finally been tested. Do not report met/missed without saying which explanation the evidence supports. Also report what the removal COST via SM-01's gap mutants, whether D3 HELD (a D3 regression outranks the D2 result), the per-channel findings-per-token ratio, and whether the instrument counts are honest now. FILE FINDINGS, FIX NOTHING.
ticket.schedule_revision_note: BUMPED TO 3, 2026-08-07, owner-agreed eval design. A lone D2 score cannot distinguish "the card works now" from "these judges were generous", so the round scores TWO SUBJECTS IN ONE PASS: the toolchain removal (a real before/after) AND a greenfield fixture re-scored (which by construction cannot reach anchor 3). If D2 separates between them, the difference is the SUBJECT and five epics of fixtures were the problem. If D2 is 2 on both, the card cannot measure complexity. SECOND AXIS: the same subjects judged at DIFFERENT MODEL TIERS. If D2 stays 2 regardless of judge strength that is strong evidence it is the card; if a stronger judge reaches anchor 3, it was judging capacity all along. COST: this expansion works against GOAL-cheaper and the round REPORTS THAT TENSION AS A RESULT, including reporting the goal MISSED if the expansion causes it. An epic that hides the cost of its own thoroughness is not measuring.
